original_question: Are the only biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces the minimal ones?
target_in_paper: Section 10.1, Conjecture 3 (the original biharmonic conjecture), rather than the broader classification Problem 12. The paper’s official formulation is: “The only biharmonic submanifolds of Euclidean spaces are the minimal ones.” ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient setting (Euclidean spaces), the right class of objects (biharmonic submanifolds), and the right proposed conclusion (minimality). It is essentially the question form of Conjecture 3 in Section 10.1. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
missing_details: The paper formulates the notion via an isometric immersion x: M^n -> E^m of a Riemannian manifold, so the question should quantify over all such immersions/submanifolds, not just use the informal phrase “submanifolds.” ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

To be stand-alone, the question should define “biharmonic” exactly as Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0, where H is the mean curvature vector field and Delta is the Laplacian on M. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

It should also define “minimal” as H identically zero; by Beltrami’s formula Delta x = -nH, this is equivalent to the immersion being harmonic (Delta x = 0). ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

The quantifier is unrestricted: the conjecture is about every biharmonic submanifold of every Euclidean space E^m, in arbitrary dimension and codimension; the extra hypotheses listed later in the paper (properly immersed, finite type, weakly convex, delta(2)-ideal, delta(3)-ideal, etc.) are only partial positive cases, not part of the conjecture itself. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

The ambient space must remain Euclidean. The nearby Remark 2 explicitly says the analogous statement is false in pseudo-Euclidean space, so the refined question should not broaden beyond Euclidean space. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

The draft is phrased as a broad classification-style question, but the nearest official paper-faithful target is the yes/no conjectural statement in Conjecture 3, not the more open-ended Problem 12 asking which nonminimal biharmonic submanifolds might exist. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
refined_question: For every isometric immersion x: M^n -> E^m of a Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space, if x is biharmonic in the sense that Delta^2 x = 0 (equivalently, Delta H = 0, where H is the mean curvature vector field), must H vanish identically? Equivalently, is every biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space minimal? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
equivalent_formulation: For every isometric immersion x: M^n -> E^m, does the biharmonic condition Delta^2 x = 0 force the harmonic/minimal condition Delta x = 0? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s original biharmonic conjecture. Section 9 defines a biharmonic immersion x: M -> E^m by Delta^2 x = 0, equivalently Delta H = 0, and recalls via Beltrami’s formula that minimality is H = 0, equivalently Delta x = 0. Section 10.1 then states Conjecture 3 exactly in the form your draft is trying to express. Problem 12 in Section 9 is broader (“Other than minimal submanifolds, which submanifolds of E^m are biharmonic?”), so Conjecture 3 is the nearest official formulation. Section 11, Remark 2 shows that keeping the ambient space Euclidean is essential, since the pseudo-Euclidean analogue is false. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

citations.label: equation (9.2): definition of biharmonic immersion; Beltrami formula (9.1) gives minimal iff harmonic ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
Remark 1 and Remark 2: conjecture remains open; pseudo-Euclidean analogue is false ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
